title: Typing async and fetch
summary: fetch() returns Promise<Response>, but TypeScript cannot infer the shape of the JSON body — you must cast it yourself. The pattern is to define an interface matching the API response, then cast the result of res.json() using as. A generic fetchJson<T> wrapper centralises this cast and makes all callers type-safe. In React, data fetching usually happens inside a useEffect or a custom hook, and the results are stored in typed state. The TMDB API, which powers the course project, returns objects with specific field names (id, title, vote_average, poster_path) — these must match the interface exactly.
keyPoints: fetch() returns Promise<Response> — TypeScript does not know the response body shape
Cast the JSON: const data = await res.json() as Movie[]
Or use a generic wrapper: async function fetchJson<T>(url: string): Promise<T>
Always check res.ok before parsing — a 404 still resolves, it does not throw
Throw on failure: if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)
async functions always return a Promise — annotate as Promise<T>, not T
TMDB fields: id, title, vote_average, poster_path — match interface names to API field names exactly

exercises.prompt: What does fetch() return in TypeScript?
exercises.explanation: fetch() is typed as returning Promise<Response>. The Response object has methods like .json(), .text(), and .ok. TypeScript does not know the shape of the body — that is your job to annotate.

exercises.prompt: How do you tell TypeScript that res.json() will return an array of Movie objects?
options: const movies = await res.json() as Movie[]
exercises.answer: const movies = await res.json() as Movie[]
exercises.explanation: res.json() returns Promise<any>. Awaiting it gives any. The as Movie[] cast narrows the type so TypeScript treats the value as Movie[]. Note: this is a compile-time cast — TypeScript trusts you; it does not validate at runtime.

exercises.prompt: A fetch to a non-existent endpoint returns a 404. In TypeScript/JavaScript, what happens by default?
options: The Promise rejects with an error
The Promise resolves with a Response where res.ok is false
exercises.answer: The Promise resolves with a Response where res.ok is false
exercises.explanation: fetch only rejects on network failure (no connection, DNS error). HTTP error codes (404, 500) still resolve. You must check res.ok and throw manually: if (!res.ok) throw new Error('...')

exercises.prompt: Which correctly types a generic fetch wrapper?
exercises.explanation: async functions always return a Promise. The return type must be Promise<T>, not T. The generic <T> lets each caller specify the expected shape: fetchJson<Movie[]>(url).

options: The interface needs to extend a base TMDB type
The field name voteAverage does not match the API's vote_average — the property will be undefined at runtime
TypeScript will error because you cannot cast API responses
exercises.answer: The field name voteAverage does not match the API's vote_average — the property will be undefined at runtime
exercises.explanation: TypeScript's cast is compile-time only — it does not transform the data. The API sends vote_average (snake_case); if your interface uses voteAverage (camelCase), the property will be undefined at runtime. Interface field names must exactly match the API field names.

exercises.prompt: Where in a React component should you call fetch to load data on mount?
options: Directly in the component body (top level)
Inside a useEffect with an empty dependency array []
exercises.answer: Inside a useEffect with an empty dependency array []
exercises.explanation: Calling fetch in the component body runs on every render. The empty dependency array [] makes useEffect run only once after the first mount — the correct place for initial data loading.

exercises.prompt: Complete the typed fetch function. It should throw if the response is not ok, and return the parsed JSON as Movie[]:
exercises.explanation: TMDB wraps the array in a results field. The return type is Promise<Movie[]>. Checking res.ok before parsing guards against silent error responses. The cast tells TypeScript the JSON shape.
